questions.question: Distinguish between renewable and non-renewable resources with two examples of each, and define sustainable development.
questions.expected_answer: Renewable resources can be replaced naturally within a human lifetime if not overused, e.g. water, soil, forests, fish, sunlight, wind. Non-renewable resources exist in fixed quantities and cannot be replaced once used, e.g. coal, crude oil, gold, platinum, iron ore. Sustainable development (Brundtland Commission, 1987): development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

questions.question: Give one sustainable practice for each sector of the economy.
questions.expected_answer: Primary (any one): crop rotation, drip irrigation, controlled grazing, fishing quotas and closed seasons, replanting forests, rehabilitating mined land. Secondary (any one): energy efficiency, solar or other renewable energy, recycling scrap materials, treating waste water, controlling air pollution. Tertiary (any one): saving electricity and paper, reducing plastic packaging, recycling e-waste, fuel-efficient transport, eco-tourism.

questions.question: Name two skills or careers needed in each sector and two routes to gaining skills.
questions.expected_answer: Primary: e.g. farmers, agricultural scientists, geologists, mining engineers, machinery operators. Secondary: e.g. artisans (electricians, welders, fitters), engineers, quality controllers, technicians. Tertiary: e.g. accountants, salespeople, programmers, nurses, teachers, chefs; people and communication skills. Routes: university, TVET colleges, learnerships and apprenticeships (SETAs), short courses.
